findings.title: No CIFAR-10 or MVTec (visual-AD) code at all — Tables 2, 4 and visual Table 5 unreproducible
findings.quote: dataset MVTec, a frozen WideResNet-50 [23] is used as the backbone for both the encoder and
findings.claim: The paper reports a full visual-AD track — CIFAR-10 image-level AUROC (Table 2, 11 classes), MVTec image/pixel-level AUROC 99.5/98.3 (Table 2), a visual ablation (Table 4) and a visual K/R sweep (Table 5) — using a DO2HSC CNN (CIFAR-10) and a frozen WideResNet-50 (MVTec). The repo contains only the tabular pipeline: a deterministic grep of all 24 .py files finds 0 references to cifar/mvtec/wideresnet/resnet/conv2d/do2hsc/torchvision, and data/ holds only 4 tabular .mat files.
findings.concern: Roughly half of the paper's headline experiments (all image results) have no code, no backbones, and no data in the repository, so they cannot be reproduced from the released artefact.
findings.resolution: Authors: release the CIFAR-10 and MVTec training/eval code, the DO2HSC-CNN and WideResNet-50 feature extractors, and the data-preparation scripts, or state that the visual experiments were run from unreleased code.

findings.title: 5 of the 20 Table-1 tabular datasets have no fetch/committed path; campaign/fraud .npz unloadable
findings.quote:
#campaign
mkdir -p data/campaign
curl -o data/campaign/5_campaign.npz https://github.com/Minqi824/ADBench/raw/main/adbench/datasets/Classical/5_campaign.npz

#fraud
mkdir -p data/fraud
curl -o data/fraud/13_fraud.npz https://github.com/Minqi824/ADBench/raw/main/adbench/datasets/Classical/13_fraud.npz
findings.claim: get_data.sh fetches 13 datasets and data/ commits 4 (glass/thyroid/wbc/wine), giving 15 distinct datasets; Table 1 lists 20. check_dataset_coverage.py shows Arrhythmia, Census, Cardiotocography, NSL-KDD and Shuttle have NO acquisition path. campaign/fraud are saved as .npz under per-dataset subdirs, but loadData() only loadmat()s a flat '<name>.mat', so even those downloads are not loadable by the shipped loader.
findings.concern: Five Table-1 rows cannot be reproduced (no data), and two more (campaign, fraud) download in a format/location the loader cannot read, so the reported 20-dataset average (78.64/91.19) cannot be recomputed as released.
findings.resolution: Authors: add the 5 missing datasets to get_data.sh (or commit them) and extend loadData() to handle the .npz ADBench format and the subdirectory layout produced by get_data.sh.

findings.title: R hardcoded to 3, K unimplemented, no ablation switches — Tables 3 (A/B/C) and 5 not reproducible
findings.claim: The number of flow modules R is hardcoded to 3 here, there is no argument anywhere for the per-module iteration count K, and each flow_unit is a fixed [AffineCoupling, ActNorm, AffineCoupling] chain (denet.py:63-65) unrelated to K. main.py always trains the full loss reconstruction_loss + 0.5*(prior_loss + post_loss) with no flag to disable RE or DE and no six-layer-MLP baseline model.
findings.concern: Table 5's 4×5 K/R sweep and Table 3's ablation variants A (baseline MLP), B (RE-only) and C (DE-only) have no corresponding code path or configuration, so those ablation numbers cannot be reproduced from the released repository.
findings.resolution: Authors: expose K and R as configurable arguments and provide the ablation-variant entrypoints (baseline MLP, RE-only, DE-only) used for Tables 3 and 5.

findings.title: prob_predictor loop does not thread z or accumulate log-det across flow modules
findings.claim: The loop iterates over all num_modules (=3) flow modules but passes the SAME z and SAME log_p_prior to every module's inverse and discards the transformed output (`_`). Only the last iteration (i=0) is returned, so log_p_post = log_p_prior + log-det of flow_net[0].inverse(z) — a single module — instead of composing F_R⁻¹∘…∘F_1⁻¹ and summing all R log-dets.
findings.concern: The density log-likelihood (Eq. 4, and hence the LMLE training term and the −α·log p(x) part of the anomaly score, Eq. 8) omits 2 of the 3 flow modules' Jacobian contributions and evaluates them at the wrong point, so the implemented density estimation is not the change-of-variables the code plainly intends.
findings.resolution: Authors: thread the transformed variable and accumulate the log-det, e.g. `for i in reversed(range(self.num_modules)): z, log_p_post = self.flow_net[i].inverse(z, log_p_post)` seeded with log_p_prior; confirm which version produced the reported numbers.

findings.title: loadData reads a hardcoded absolute path /home/author/ddpm/UniINN/data/ — crashes for anyone else
findings.claim: Every dataset is loaded from the author's absolute path '/home/author/ddpm/UniINN/data/<name>.mat', ignoring the repo's own Unifying_INN/data/ directory.
findings.concern: The only entrypoint (main.py) calls loadData for all tabular datasets, so the entire tabular pipeline — Tables 1, 3 and 5 — raises FileNotFoundError on any machine other than the author's, and even after fixing the path the committed data lives at Unifying_INN/data/ while get_data.sh writes to data/<name>/<file>.
findings.resolution: Authors: replace the absolute path with a repo-relative / CLI-configurable data directory and align it with get_data.sh's output layout.

findings.title: Misspelled attribute cudnn.deterministirc silently disables the determinism flag
findings.claim: setup_seed sets torch.backends.cudnn.deterministirc (typo for 'deterministic'), which creates a no-op attribute rather than enabling cuDNN determinism.
findings.concern: Intended deterministic cuDNN behaviour is never actually turned on, so GPU runs may not be reproducible despite the fixed seed; the effect is minor but the guard silently does nothing.
findings.resolution: Authors: fix the spelling to torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True.

findings.title: Released flow uses affine coupling (RealNVP); the Eq.2 i-DenseNet contraction unit is dead code
findings.claim: Each flow_unit is built from AffineCoupling + ActNorm + AffineCoupling (standard RealNVP). The _iMonotoneBlock closure — which wraps iMonotoneBlock, the invertible-monotone-operator unit implementing the paper's Eq. 2 contraction mapping f(x)=((Id+G)/2)⁻¹(x)−x via an i-DenseNet (iMonotoneBlock.py:51-65) — is defined but never appended to the chain and is unused everywhere (grep: only its own definition).
findings.concern: The paper's entire theory (Definition 1, Lemmas 1-2, Propositions 1-2, Fig. 1/3/4 'fixed point in the normal manifold' mechanism) rests on the map being a contraction with Lipschitz constant <1; an affine-coupling layer's Jacobian scale exp(0.5·tanh(·)) can exceed 1, so the released model is not a contraction mapping and does not instantiate the paper's central contribution.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether Tables 1-5 were produced by the affine-coupling model in this repo or by the iMonotoneBlock/i-DenseNet path; if the latter, release that configuration.

findings.title: aucPerformance reports max AUROC/AP over {s, −s, |s|, s²} scored against the test labels
findings.claim: The reported AUROC/AP is the maximum over four transforms of the anomaly score — score, −score, |score|, score² — each evaluated against the ground-truth test labels; aucPerformance is the metric used by evaluation_batch (main.py:49) for the reported numbers.
findings.concern: Choosing the score orientation/transform that maximises the metric on the test labels is test-set label leakage: because roc_auc(labels,−s)=1−roc_auc(labels,s), every reported AUROC is bounded below by 0.5 and is upward-biased (check_auc_orientation.py: an anti-correlated score with honest AUROC 0.18 is reported as 0.82; pure noise reports 0.52), so Table 1/3 AUROC and AP are not honest fixed-orientation metrics.
findings.resolution: Authors: fix the anomaly-score orientation a priori (higher = more anomalous, per Eq. 8) and report roc_auc_score(labels, score) without the max-over-transforms; re-report Tables 1 and 3.

findings.title: No validation set; K,R (Table 5) and epoch are selected on the test set
findings.quote:
train_x = normal_data[ixs[:n_train]]
train_y = normal_labels[ixs[:n_train]]
anomalous_data = features[np.where(labels==1)[0]][:]
anomalous_labels = labels[np.where(labels==1)[0]]
test_x = np.concatenate((anomalous_data, normal_data_test), axis=0)
test_y = np.concatenate((anomalous_labels, normal_labels_test), axis=0)
findings.claim: loadData returns only train and test splits — no validation set is ever created. main.py evaluates on the test loader every 5 epochs (main.py:82-85), and Table 5 selects the 'best' K,R (K=2,R=3) by their AP/AUROC on the same tabular/MVTec test sets.
findings.concern: With no held-out validation data, the reported best K/R (and the epoch at which test AUROC is read) are chosen using test-set performance, which optimistically biases the headline 78.64/91.19; the ambiguity is that the config might instead have been fixed a priori from prior work.
findings.resolution: Authors: hold out a validation split from the training normals for model/hyperparameter selection, or confirm that K,R,λ,α were fixed without consulting test-set metrics.
